name: beifahrer
description: Beifahrer — let an AI agent ride along in the browser you already use (Firefox, Chromium), under a per-site policy you control. A WebExtension plus an MCP server that runs on GJS via gjsify.

scripts.build: gjsify workspace beifahrer-app build && gjsify workspace beifahrer-extension build

listing.singlePurpose: Lets the person's own AI agent use their own browser, under a per-site policy that the person sets and can pause at any time.

permissions.tabs: Reads the URL and title of open tabs, to apply the per-site policy to the tab the agent addresses and to list tabs to the person.
permissions.storage: Stores the person's per-site policy, feature switches, pairing token and pause state in the browser's local extension storage.
permissions.alarms: Wakes the background worker to reconnect to the local bridge, save the automatic session snapshot, and end temporary site access when it expires.
permissions.sessions: Lists and restores recently closed tabs and windows, only when the person has switched tab management on.
permissions.tabGroups: Names and colours tab groups, only when the person has switched tab management on.
permissions.scripting: Injects the page agent that reads and acts on a page, only after the policy allows that site's origin.
permissions.offscreen: Opens an empty offscreen document that reads the browser's light/dark colour scheme, so the toolbar icon matches it.
permissions.webRequest: Optional. Lists network requests of a tab so the agent can see why a button did nothing; requested only when the person switches it on.
permissions.downloads: Optional. Captures a page as a file for the agent; requested only when the person switches it on, and used only for that capture.
permissions.http://*/*: Optional. Access to a site is requested per host when the person raises that site above "none"; the temporary "all sites" grant uses this pattern.
permissions.https://*/*: Optional. Access to a site is requested per host when the person raises that site above "none"; the temporary "all sites" grant uses this pattern.
permissions.<all_urls>: Optional. Needed only for screenshots, because the browser's capture call accepts nothing narrower; requested when the person switches screenshots on.

components.name: Beifahrer
components.summary: The app: a window that shows your agents, browsers and pairing token, and the MCP server your coding agent connects to. Open it and follow the setup assistant.

components.name: Browser extension
components.summary: Beifahrer's half inside the browser. Pair it with the app using the token the app shows.
